source_caption:
The stunning architectural masterpiece where the wealthy Park family lives wasn’t an actual home. Director Bong Joon Ho had the entire house meticulously built from scratch on an open lot, specifically designing the structure around the sun’s path to ensure the natural lighting perfectly highlighted the film’s simmering class tension.
⠀
Parasite (2019), directed by Bong Joon Ho, starring Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong. A destitute family cleverly infiltrates the glamorous lives of a wealthy household, leading to a darkly comedic and devastating collision of class warfare.
⠀

source_details.title: Parasite
source_details.synopsis: Parasite (Korean: 기생충) is a 2019 South Korean black comedy thriller film directed by Bong Joon Ho, who co-wrote the screenplay with Han Jin-won. It stars Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong, Choi Woo-shik, Park So-dam, Jang Hye-jin, Park Myung-hoon, and Lee Jung-eun. The film follows a poor family who infiltrate the home and life of a wealthy family. The script is based on a play Bong wrote in 2013. He later adapted it into a 15-page film draft, which was split into three different drafts by Han. Bong said he was inspired by the Korean film The Housemaid (1960) and the 1930s Christine and Léa Papin incident. Filming ran from May to September 2018 and included cinematographer Hong Kyung
